Counsel for Applicant :- Ramakar Shukla,Subodh Kumar Pandey Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA and perused the record.
2. The applicant seeks enlargement on bail in FIR No.162 of 2022, under Section 498A, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, P.S. Mailani, District Lakhimpur Kheri.

3. In terms of the FIR it was alleged that the daughter of the informant was married to the applicant around five years ago, however, demands of dowry were being made and subsequently on Bhupendra vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

sentences.text:
on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124455141/
1 04.05.2022, the daughter of the informant was killed.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant draws my attention to the post-mortem report which indicates the cause of death as ante mortem hanging and apart from the ligature mark, two abrasions are seen on the left elbow and left knee.
In the light of the said, it is argued by counsel for the applicant that the applicant who is in custody since 09.05.2022 and has no criminal antecedent may be enlarged on bail.

5. Learned AGA has opposed the bail application by arguing that apart from the ligature mark, two injuries were also visible on the body of the victim, as such, the applicant who is the husband should not be granted bail.

6. Considering the submissions made at the Bar, prima-facie, apart from the ligature mark, two minor injuries are revealed on the body of the victim which are on the left elbow and left knee, and there is no material to demonstrate that soon before the death, the victim was subjected to physical or mental harassment in relation to demand of dowry leading to the death and also considering the fact that the applicant is in custody since 09.05.2022 and has no criminal antecedent, as such, the applicant is entitled to be enlarged on bail.
In view thereof, the application is allowed.

7. Let the applicant Bhupendra be released on bail in aforesaid FIR number on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
Order Date :- 16.1.2024 nishant  Bhupendra vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.
